status: Procedural design specification, not measured reproductions or construction documents.
basis: Six primary architectural/photo sources establish a material and massing vocabulary. All numerical dimensions, city ratios, service details, hybrids and palette values below are design proposals inferred for this scene; they are not dimensions measured from the referenced buildings. Some references predate 1970 and are used as antecedents for 1970s-1990s city fabric.
coordinates: Each footprint is [street frontage width, plot depth]. y=up. Front is negative local z. Floors include ground level; height = groundFloor + (storeys-1)*typicalFloor, excluding parapet/crown. Bay is facade module; divide available facade width into a nearest whole count and preserve end piers.

sources.title: Boston City Hall Study Report, City of Boston
sources.evidence: City describes massive concrete Brutalist form completed in 1968. Report search excerpt identifies 2023 west-elevation photograph with repetitive bays, recessed central entrance and brick plaza. Documented vocabulary: brick lower levels, articulated concrete upper levels, civic forecourt.
sources.access: Official HTML read; large photo report endpoint was too large for full tool extraction. Use this as documented architectural evidence, not a dimensional survey.

sources.title: The Portland Building, Michael Graves
sources.evidence: Architect documents 1982 completion, emphatic color and ornament, legible base/middle/top and large entrance columns. Page provides built-building and facade-detail photographs. Use organized color fields, small punched openings, oversized portal and cornice; do not duplicate sculpture or exact composition.

sources.title: Lever House, SOM
sources.evidence: Architect documents blue-green glass, stainless steel, two intersecting horizontal and vertical masses, a two-story base and public plaza. It explicitly identifies the building as an antecedent for later downtown office construction. Useful distinctions: thin curtain-wall members, flush glass, opaque spandrel bands, exposed ground-level columns.

sources.title: Sunnyvale strip mall, photograph by Yngvadottir
sources.evidence: Own-work photograph identifies a strip mall on Hollenbeck Avenue, Sunnyvale. Low shop row and forecourt provide commercial-edge reference. Detailed clinic, laboratory and service-building forms below are original programmatic extrapolations, not claims about this photograph.

sources.title: Edificio Diego Portales, Santiago, photograph by Rodrigo Fernandez
sources.evidence: Own-work 2014 photograph identifies the Santiago office tower while in Ministry of Defense use. Provides a real Latin American modernist slab reference. Below, closely repeated vertical members and a long narrow slab are a procedural interpretation, not a measured reconstruction.

sources.title: Government Center Garage, Boston, photograph by Gunnar Klack
sources.evidence: Own-work March 2014 photograph documents the garage while intact. Use open dark parking floors bounded by structural concrete and parapets as garage vocabulary; the scene must depict maintained operating structure, not demolition.

urbanRules.designIntent: Empty, maintained, sun-faded city. Silence comes from absent occupancy and repetition with occasional mismatches; avoid ruin cues.

downtownBlocks.plazaFrequency: One deliberate 18-28 wide plaza cut per 2-3 blocks; do not give every tower a plaza.
downtownBlocks.placement: Place some 8-12 floor buildings directly between 20-30 floor towers. Let frontage bases meet the sidewalk while upper volumes vary. Rotate two-thirds of long slabs parallel to block edge and one-third perpendicular. Keep a clear skyline hierarchy.

edgeBlocks.placement: Group 3-5 low buildings into a coherent commercial frontage; put service courts behind and between them. Occasional taller telecom or laboratory acts as a transition. Do not scatter lone boxes evenly.

streets.visualRule: Simple empty lanes and intact faded markings. Keep consecutive intersections visibly aligned over 3-5 blocks for scale and unease.

props.placement: curb zone; paired only on broad arterial; alternate sides on secondary streets
major crossings; signal heads deliberately face roadway
limited groups at service entries and plazas
one near selected intersections, never random in walkway
one every 2-3 blocks; thin steel, green glass, empty bench, no ads with people
isolated plaza edge; sparse clipped shrubs, not overgrowth
group by service core; visible only above low parapets; never uniform on every roof

aging.rule: Use subtle streaks below joints, dusty sill edges, repaint rectangles, faint paving patches. Keep glazing whole, roofs straight, storefronts intact, rails upright and entrances usable.

avoid: all towers identical prisms with recolored windows
dark glass stamped on concrete planes without frame or recess
arbitrary facade lines unrelated to floor height
all buildings standing in isolated lawns
demolition scars, collapsed roofs, boarded windows, vines or debris fields
dense props distributed as random noise
bright cyan glazing or mirror-metal concrete
all towers sharing exactly the same parapet and roof box

implementationPriority: Preserve the 32 distinct massing/facade/ground-interface combinations even when simplifying mesh counts.
Build readable silhouette and human-scale access first: podium, canopy, ramp, arcade, stair, shutter, open garage slots.
At close range, make window recesses real: frame planes in front of dark glass; deep concrete cells need horizontal soffit/sill and vertical reveals.
At distance, collapse repeated windows into instanced quads or atlas grids but retain corner piers, setbacks, crowns and large fins as geometry.
Use per-building deterministic seeds with coherent bands of subtle color variation. Do not randomize every pane independently.
Group structural modules with instanced meshes by material; reserve higher segment counts for the single spiral garage and ramp/rail curves.
Material roughness and restrained brightness need to survive neutral overcast/daylight; ambient occlusion at recesses matters more than grunge textures.
For pedestrian camera use 1.65-1.75 eye height, 65-75 degree vertical FOV and 0.15 curb as immediate scale cues. Avoid a miniature aerial framing for final review.
